cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: See What This Took
cards.instruction: Make someone recognize the courage, restraint, or emotional labor your choices required.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Compare the angry letter with the one I sent. Notice the crossing-out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I appreciate the apology you sent. Why show me the angry version?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Because 'sorry' took ten minutes. Not sending the rest took all night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now I'm tempted to read what you spared me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please admire the thickness with it shut. I'd like one night's restraint to survive breakfast.

mechanism: A permits admiration of withheld anger while restricting access to it, seeking credit for restraint from an authoritative curator position.
confusable: D75 names hurt caused by an event; D105 asks recognition of the effort required by A chosen restraint.
comparison: An unsent angry draft differs from a committee refusal made without an excuse.
seedUse: Use D105-a ten-minute apology versus all-night restraint and B curiosity; keep the actual angry contents unneeded.
